name: Adult Beginner Course
description: This course is the natural starting point for adults aged sixteen and over who have never picked up a padel bat, and it welcomes both men and women onto the same court. Twice a week, Layla Nasser walks newcomers through the fundamentals: grip, positioning, glass rebounds, serving and the underarm technique that separates padel from tennis. Sessions blend short technical drills with plenty of live points, so confidence builds quickly alongside the strokes themselves. Expect to learn how to read the walls, construct a rally patiently, and understand the scoring system without feeling rushed. Layla keeps groups small and mixed in ability, pairing newer faces with slightly steadier hands so everyone gets time on the ball. Bring court shoes with non-marking soles, a bottle of water, and a padel bat if you own one; loan bats are available for those still deciding. Comfortable sportswear suited to warm evenings is recommended throughout the programme.

name: Adult Improver Course
description: Baseline Al Quoz's Adult Improver Course is built for mixed players aged 16 and above who already have padel fundamentals in place and want to sharpen them under proper coaching structure. Running early on Saturday mornings, sessions move briskly through a warm-up, technical drilling, and live points play, giving everyone a chance to test new skills against real match situations. Expect focused work on volley consistency, smash placement, and reading the glass, along with a good dose of tactical positioning for doubles play. Coaches rotate pairings throughout so you're always challenged by different styles and paces. This course suits intermediate players comfortable rallying but wanting more control, variety, and court awareness. Bring a padel racket, indoor court shoes with non-marking soles, and a bottle of water, as the courts warm up quickly even in the early slot. Bibs and balls are provided. Turn up ten minutes early for a proper warm-up and to settle in before the session starts.

name: Ladies Beginner Academy
description: Ladies Beginner Academy at Baseline Al Quoz is a relaxed, ladies-only introduction to padel, open to anyone aged sixteen and over with no upper limit. Sessions run every Friday from four until half past five, giving newcomers a full ninety minutes to build real confidence on court. Coaches start with the basics: how to hold the racket, court positioning, and the underarm serve, before moving into simple rallies against the glass and gentle scoring drills. Each week layers on the last, so participants steadily pick up shot selection, movement between the lines, and basic doubles tactics without ever feeling rushed or overwhelmed. The atmosphere is supportive and social, with small group sizes ensuring plenty of individual feedback. Bring comfortable sports clothing, a pair of non-marking court shoes, and a bottle of water; rackets are provided for anyone who doesn't yet own one. Ideal for complete beginners, returning players, or anyone wanting a friendly, low-pressure way to learn the sport alongside other women.

name: Ladies Social Doubles
description: Ladies Social Doubles at Baseline Al Quoz brings together a friendly group of women players for a lively Friday evening on court, running from 19:00 to 20:30. This session is designed for intermediate players aged 18 and over, with no upper age limit, and is exclusively for ladies. Expect a warm-up followed by rotating doubles matches, where our coach offers light guidance on positioning, shot selection, and net play without turning the evening into a formal lesson. It's the ideal setting to sharpen tactical awareness, build consistency on your volleys and smashes, and get comfortable reading the game alongside players of a similar standard. Beyond the padel itself, it's a great way to meet other women in the community, unwind after the working week, and enjoy some competitive but relaxed rallies under the evening lights. Bring your own racket if you have one, comfortable court shoes, and water. Rackets are available to borrow for those who need one.

name: Junior Academy
description: Junior Academy at Baseline Al Quoz is a beginner programme for boys and girls aged 9 to 15, welcoming complete newcomers to padel as well as juniors with a little racket-sport background. Sessions run twice a week, with coaches splitting the court into small groups so every player gets plenty of contact time with the ball. Early weeks focus on grip, the underarm serve, and reading the bounce off the glass, before progressing into simple rallies, positioning at the net, and the basics of scoring. Coaches place a strong emphasis on footwork and court awareness, building habits that carry through to matchplay later on. Sessions are lively and games-based, mixing drills with point-play so young players stay engaged while learning proper technique. Juniors should bring a padel or tennis racket if they own one, indoor court shoes, a refillable water bottle, and sun protection for the walk between the car park and courts. Rackets are available to borrow for beginners without their own.

name: Junior Performance Squad
description: Junior Performance Squad is a twice-weekly programme for competitive-minded players aged 12 to 17, open to boys and girls of intermediate level. Held on Tuesday and Thursday evenings at Baseline Al Quoz, sessions run from 20:30 to 22:00 under floodlights once the day's heat has eased. Each class opens with movement and footwork drills before progressing into pressure-based rally patterns, positional play at the net, and match-tempo points designed to sharpen decision-making. Coaches focus on smash technique, lob discipline, and reading an opponent's shape, with regular video review used to reinforce lessons learned on court. The group format encourages friendly competition, with rotating pairs and short internal ladders to keep intensity high. This class suits juniors already comfortable with rallying who want structured progression toward tournament-level play. Bring court shoes with non-marking soles, a padel racket, water, and a light change of clothing, as the session is physically demanding. Rackets are available to hire at reception for those without their own.

name: Kids Padel Starters
description: Kids Padel Starters at Baseline Al Quoz is a friendly introduction to the sport for boys and girls aged 5 to 8, run every Sunday and Thursday from 09:00 to 10:30. Sessions are built around fun, movement and coordination rather than competition, with coaches using scaled-down rackets, softer balls and mini-court zones to keep things safe and manageable for little beginners. Children will learn the basics of grip, simple forehand and backhand taps, underarm serving, and how to move around the court with balance and control. Group games and relay-style drills keep energy high and attention spans engaged, while coaches gently introduce court awareness and teamwork. This class suits complete beginners and those with only minimal racket-sport experience. Please bring comfortable sports clothing, closed-toe trainers, a labelled water bottle and sun protection, as parts of the warm-up may take place outdoors before moving to the court. Rackets are provided, though children are welcome to bring their own if they have one.

name: Cardio Padel
description: Cardio Padel at Baseline Al Quoz is a high-energy, fitness-first session built around constant movement rather than match tactics. Expect a brisk warm-up followed by rotating drill stations, quickfire rallies, and short-court games designed to keep your heart rate up and your feet busy for the full ninety minutes. It's open to all levels and mixed genders, welcoming anyone aged sixteen and upward, so newcomers can work alongside seasoned players without feeling out of place. Coaches focus on movement efficiency, split-step timing, and shot repetition under fatigue, meaning you'll leave with sharper reactions and better court coverage rather than a stack of new tactics to memorise. It suits players wanting a proper workout with a racket in hand, or anyone easing into padel through activity rather than instruction. Bring court shoes with non-marking soles, a padel racket if you own one, and a water bottle, since spares are limited. Sessions run every Saturday and Monday from four until half five in the afternoon.

name: Competition Squad
description: Competition Squad at Baseline Al Quoz is built for advanced mixed players aged sixteen and up who are chasing tournament form. Under Nicolas Prado's guidance, sessions running Sunday and Tuesday evenings from 16:00 to 17:30 focus on match simulation, high-intensity point play and the fine margins that decide close sets: bandeja depth, smash placement, and reading an opponent's shoulder before the ball arrives. Expect structured drills that bleed into live scoring, with video-style feedback delivered courtside rather than off it. This squad suits players already competing locally who want sharper decision-making under pressure and a training group that pushes pace every week. Bring indoor and outdoor-rated padel shoes, a racket you already trust in matches, water, and a willingness to be corrected in front of the group. Numbers are kept small so every player gets genuine court time against opponents of comparable standard.

name: Technique Clinic
description: Technique Clinic is a focused, intermediate-level mixed session for players sixteen and older who want to rebuild their strokes from the ground up rather than just play more matches. Coach Hana Kimura runs these evening sessions on Monday and Wednesday from 20:30 to 22:00, breaking down grip, contact point and body rotation for the core padel shots: the volley, the bandeja, the vibora and the serve. Expect plenty of repetition against fed balls, slow-motion shadow swings, and small corrections repeated until they stick. Participants typically leave with a clearer sense of why a shot is misfiring, not just that it is. This class suits club players who have the basics but want technical precision before stepping up to competitive play. Bring your own racket, indoor court shoes, and a notebook or phone for the odd technical cue worth remembering between sessions.

name: Morning Social Drills
description: Morning Social Drills brings mixed players of every level together for an easygoing but structured start to the day at Baseline Al Quoz. Running Sunday and Tuesday from 07:00 to 08:30 under coach Rashid Al Blooshi, the session rotates pairs through drills covering positioning, wall play and simple attacking patterns, with the emphasis firmly on movement and enjoyment rather than intensity. Open to anyone aged sixteen and above regardless of experience, it is designed so a first-time player and a seasoned club regular can share a court comfortably. Expect warm-up rallies, cooperative drills, and a relaxed mini-tournament to close things out most weeks. It suits early risers who want their padel done before the day gets busy and a social crowd to share it with. Bring a racket if you own one, otherwise loan rackets are available, along with comfortable indoor shoes and a water bottle.

name: Tactics Workshop
description: Tactics Workshop is an advanced mixed session for players eighteen and over who already have solid technique and want to sharpen their court sense instead. Held Tuesday and Thursday evenings from 19:00 to 20:30 with Nicolas Prado, the class works through positional patterns, when to attack the middle, how to exploit the lob against a poor overhead, and the timing of net transitions as a pair. Much of the session is played out in live points with pauses to reset formations and discuss options, so participants leave understanding not just what to do but why. It suits competitive players who feel technically capable but occasionally lost tactically during matches. A training partner familiar with doubles structure will help but is not required, as pairings rotate. Bring a racket, non-marking indoor shoes, and water, and come ready to talk through decisions as much as play them out.

name: Adult Beginner Course
description: Adult Beginner Course is the natural starting point for anyone aged sixteen and above who has never picked up a padel racket or has played only a handful of times. Coach Rashid Al Blooshi leads these mixed sessions on Monday and Wednesday evenings from 20:30 to 22:00, covering the fundamentals in a patient, structured order: grip and ready position, the underarm serve, basic volleys, and how to use the glass and mesh walls without panicking the first time the ball bounces off them. Scoring and court etiquette are introduced gradually so newcomers feel comfortable playing socially by the end of the course. Small group sizes mean plenty of individual correction alongside partner drills. This course suits complete beginners of any age from sixteen upwards who want a genuinely low-pressure introduction. Rackets are available to borrow, so new participants only need to bring indoor sports shoes, water, and comfortable clothing.

name: Adult Improver Course
description: Adult Improver Course is aimed at intermediate mixed players aged sixteen and up who have the basics down and are ready to build consistency and tactical awareness. Running Monday and Wednesday mornings from 07:00 to 08:30 with coach Tomas Aguirre, sessions move beyond simple rallying into court positioning, the bandeja and smash, and early doubles strategy such as when to hold the net and when to retreat. Drills alternate between technical repetition and live points so improvements get tested under real match conditions straight away. Participants generally arrive already comfortable with a rally and a serve, looking to iron out inconsistencies and start winning more points through decision-making rather than luck. It suits players who have finished a beginner course or built similar experience socially. Bring your own racket where possible, indoor court shoes, and water, as the early time slot moves quickly once the group is warmed up.

name: Ladies Beginner Academy
description: Ladies Beginner Academy offers women aged sixteen and above a dedicated, unhurried introduction to padel in a ladies-only environment. Coach Layla Nasser runs these sessions on Wednesday and Saturday from 17:30 to 19:00, working through grip, footwork, the underarm serve and basic wall rebounds at a pace suited to complete newcomers. The atmosphere is deliberately supportive, with plenty of paired practice and encouragement rather than pressure, so participants build confidence alongside technique. By the end of the course most players are comfortable serving, rallying and understanding basic scoring well enough to join social matches elsewhere at the club. It suits women who are new to racket sports entirely as much as those returning after time away from sport. Loan rackets are available for anyone who does not yet own one; participants should bring indoor sports shoes, water, and light layers for the air-conditioned courts.

name: Ladies Social Doubles
description: Ladies Social Doubles is a weekly intermediate session reserved for women aged eighteen and over who already play regularly and want competitive doubles in a relaxed, ladies-only setting. Held Friday from 17:30 to 19:00 with coach Layla Nasser, the format leans towards rotated doubles matches rather than heavy drilling, with light coaching input on positioning, shot selection and communication between partners as points unfold. It suits players who have moved past beginner technique and want consistent match play against a similar standard, alongside a social group that plays together most weeks. Expect a warm-up rally, rotating pairings across several matches, and informal feedback on patterns that worked or broke down. Newcomers to the group are welcome provided they are comfortable rallying and scoring independently. Bring your own racket, appropriate indoor court shoes, and water, and expect a sociable hour and a half that still keeps the padel genuinely competitive.

name: Junior Academy
description: Junior Academy is the entry point for young players aged 9 to 15, open to boys and girls with little or no padel experience. Under Omar Farouk's guidance, sessions running on Saturday and Monday evenings focus on the basics: grip, footwork, wall rebounds, and safe court movement, all introduced through games and progressive drills rather than repetitive lectures. Omar keeps groups small enough that every junior gets hands-on correction, and the pace is built around confidence first, technique second. Expect plenty of rallying practice and simple scoring rules explained along the way, so newcomers leave understanding not just how to hit the ball but how a point actually unfolds. Bring court shoes with non-marking soles, a water bottle, and a padel racket if owned, though loan rackets are available on request. Light, breathable clothing is recommended given the evening heat. Parents are welcome to observe from the seating area throughout the 90-minute session.

name: Junior Performance Squad
description: Junior Performance Squad is designed for competitively minded players aged 12 to 17 who already have a beginner foundation and want to sharpen match-ready skills. Coached by Omar Farouk on Sunday and Thursday evenings, sessions move beyond basics into consistent groundstrokes, controlled volleys, smash timing, and reading the glass for rebound angles. Omar structures each 90-minute block around live points and situational drills, pushing juniors to make faster decisions under light pressure while correcting technical habits as they emerge. Tactical concepts such as court positioning and shot selection are introduced progressively, preparing squad members for club-level matches and future tournament play. This mixed group welcomes both boys and girls at intermediate level. Bring a padel racket, non-marking court shoes, and a refillable water bottle; a spare shirt is useful given the intensity of the drills. Consistent attendance is encouraged, as sessions build on skills covered the previous week.

name: Kids Padel Starters
description: Kids Padel Starters introduces the youngest players, aged 5 to 8, to their first taste of the sport in a relaxed, playful setting. Sofia Marchetti leads these Sunday and Thursday afternoon sessions with an emphasis on coordination, balance, and simple hand-eye games before a racket is even picked up properly. Children learn to hold the racket correctly, make gentle contact with soft foam balls, and understand basic court boundaries, all through activities designed to keep attention spans engaged for the full 90 minutes. Sofia's approach favours encouragement over correction at this age, building enthusiasm and comfort on court that will support later technical learning. This mixed group welcomes both boys and girls. Bring comfortable trainers, a labelled water bottle, and a sun hat if the session runs before shaded hours. Rackets are provided for this age group, so no equipment purchase is necessary before the first visit.

name: Cardio Padel
description: Cardio Padel is an energetic, fitness-focused class open to adults of all standards, from complete beginners to seasoned players looking for a different kind of workout. Sofia Marchetti runs these Tuesday and Thursday morning sessions at a brisk pace, blending padel strokes with continuous movement patterns, shadow drills, and short high-intensity rallies rather than formal match play. The emphasis sits on heart rate and mobility as much as technique, though participants naturally sharpen reaction speed and shot consistency along the way. Groups are mixed gender and mixed ability, with Sofia adjusting intensity so newer players and fitter regulars can train side by side comfortably. Expect a proper sweat by the end of the 90 minutes. Bring supportive court shoes, a full water bottle, a towel, and a racket if owned, as loan equipment is limited during this particular class. Open to anyone aged 16 and above.

name: Competition Squad
description: Competition Squad is the most demanding class on offer, built for advanced adult players preparing for tournaments or high-level club matches. Diego Fernandez leads this Friday evening session with a sharp focus on match simulation, advanced tactics, and the fine margins that separate good players from competitive ones, including serve variation, lob defence, and net pressure combinations. Sessions move quickly between structured drills and live scored points, with Diego offering direct feedback on shot selection and positioning as play unfolds. This mixed group is open to men and women aged 16 and above who already play at an advanced level and want targeted preparation rather than general coaching. Expect a physically and mentally intense 90 minutes. Bring a racket suited to competitive play, non-marking court shoes, and adequate hydration, as rest breaks are kept short to mirror match conditions. Prior playing experience is expected before joining this squad.

name: Technique Clinic
description: Technique Clinic offers focused, detail-driven coaching for intermediate adult players who already understand the game but want to refine specific strokes. Tomas Aguirre runs these Tuesday and Thursday morning sessions around a rotating curriculum covering topics such as bandeja and vibora execution, backhand consistency, and precise wall and glass reads. Rather than open play, the format favours repetition drills, video-style shadow feedback, and small-group correction, giving each participant close attention on the mechanics holding their game back. Tomas breaks movements down methodically, so players leave each 90-minute clinic with a clear, practised adjustment rather than a vague list of tips. This mixed class welcomes adults aged 16 and above at intermediate level. Bring a racket, non-marking court shoes, and a water bottle; a notebook is optional but many players find it useful to track the technical points raised across sessions.

name: Adult Improver Course
description: Adult Improver Course suits players aged 16 and above who have grasped the basics and are ready to tighten up technique and tactical awareness. Miguel Santana leads these early Monday and Wednesday morning sessions with a practical mix of stroke refinement, positioning work, and controlled point play, targeting common intermediate sticking points such as inconsistent volleys, weak second serves, and hesitant net approaches. Miguel structures the 90 minutes around progressive drills that build toward realistic match situations, giving this mixed group plenty of live-ball practice alongside technical correction. Participants can expect steady, honest feedback aimed at breaking bad habits before they become permanent. Early starts suit those wanting to train before work commitments take over the day. Bring a racket, non-marking court shoes, and water; a light layer is useful given the cooler morning temperatures on court before the sun is fully up.

name: Ladies Beginner Academy
description: This ladies-only beginner academy at Baseline JVC is designed for women aged sixteen and above who are picking up a racket for the first time or returning after a long break. Running on Saturday evenings, sessions with coach Fatima Al Zaabi focus on the fundamentals: grip, the underarm serve, wall rebounds, and understanding the glass and mesh that make padel distinct from tennis. Fatima builds a relaxed, encouraging atmosphere so newcomers feel comfortable making mistakes while learning positioning and simple doubles tactics. Over successive weeks, participants progress from static drills to light rallying and eventually short points, building confidence alongside a supportive group of peers at a similar stage. Bring a padel or tennis-style racket if you own one, though loan rackets are available, along with non-marking indoor or court trainers, a bottle of water, and light layers, since the pace builds gradually but steadily across the ninety-minute session.

name: Ladies Social Doubles
description: Held twice weekly on Wednesday and Saturday evenings, Ladies Social Doubles at Baseline JVC is an intermediate-level, ladies-only session for women eighteen and over who already understand the basics and want regular, competitive match play. Coach Fatima Al Zaabi organises rotating doubles fixtures so players face different partners and opponents each week, sharpening net play, lob accuracy, and communication within a pair. Expect a short warm-up and tactical pointer before games begin, with Fatima offering feedback between sets on shot selection and court positioning. It is a sociable format that still pushes technical improvement, ideal for those wanting consistency rather than one-off drop-ins. Bring your own racket, comfortable court shoes, and a water bottle; a change of top is worthwhile given the pace of matches. Newcomers to the group are welcome provided they are comfortable rallying and scoring points already.
