name: Junior Performance Squad
description: Junior Performance Squad is an intermediate, mixed-gender programme at Baseline JVC for young players aged twelve to seventeen who already have solid padel foundations and want to train more seriously. Sessions run early Monday and Wednesday mornings under coach Karim Mansour, structured around footwork patterns, wall-play repetition, smash technique, and doubles tactics such as switching and covering the middle. Karim introduces video-style feedback discussions and situational drills that mimic match pressure, preparing juniors for club competitions and tournament play. Fitness elements are woven into the warm-up to build the movement and reaction speed padel demands. This squad suits committed juniors looking to bridge the gap between recreational play and competitive standard. Bring a well-strung racket, appropriate court shoes, a change of shirt, and a substantial water bottle given the early start and intensity. Parents should ensure juniors have eaten beforehand, as sessions are physically demanding from the outset.

name: Kids Padel Starters
description: Kids Padel Starters at Baseline JVC is a gentle, mixed-gender introduction for children aged five to eight, held on Sunday and Tuesday evenings under coach Karim Mansour. Sessions favour games, coordination exercises, and oversized targets over formal drilling, helping the youngest players develop balance, ball tracking, and basic racket control in a fun, low-pressure environment. Karim uses simplified scoring and shortened courts so children experience rallying and scoring points early, building enthusiasm for the sport before technical correction begins in earnest. Parents can expect plenty of encouragement and structured play rather than repetitive technique work at this stage. It is an ideal starting point for children with no prior racket sport experience. Please send children in comfortable sports clothing and trainers, with a labelled water bottle, and a lightweight racket if the family owns one, though junior-sized loan rackets are provided for those who do not.

name: Cardio Padel
description: Cardio Padel at Baseline JVC is an all-levels, mixed-gender fitness-focused session for adults sixteen and above, running early Monday and Wednesday mornings with coach Elena Popova. Rather than emphasising technical refinement, sessions combine padel-specific movement patterns, continuous rallying drills, and interval-style conditioning to raise heart rate and improve overall court fitness. Elena structures each class around rotating drill stations so participants of mixed ability keep moving throughout, touching on shot repetition, footwork ladders, and short competitive points as a cooldown. It suits players who want an energetic start to the day and a workout alongside their padel practice, regardless of prior experience. Expect to sweat, and expect friendly camaraderie among a regular group of early risers. Bring proper court trainers, a full water bottle, a towel, and a spare shirt, since the early morning slot moves briskly from the very first whistle.

name: Competition Squad
description: Competition Squad at Baseline JVC is an advanced, mixed-gender training group for adults sixteen and over who compete or intend to compete in club and regional tournaments, running Monday and Wednesday mid-mornings with coach Andres Rivas. Sessions concentrate on high-level tactics: shot disguise, aggressive net positioning, smash variations, and reading opponents' patterns during extended points. Andres incorporates match simulation and situational scoring so players experience tournament pressure within training, followed by detailed tactical debriefs. This squad expects a strong existing technical base and genuine competitive intent, with places typically limited to maintain training quality. Physical conditioning is folded into drills rather than treated separately, so expect a demanding pace throughout. Bring a well-maintained racket, spare grips if you use them, indoor or all-court trainers, and ample water, since sessions run at high intensity for the full ninety minutes with minimal breaks between drills.

name: Technique Clinic
description: Technique Clinic at Baseline JVC is an intermediate, mixed-gender session for adults sixteen and above who want focused, detailed correction of their padel strokes, running Monday and Wednesday evenings with coach Miguel Santana. Rather than match play, the clinic isolates specific elements of technique each week, such as the bandeja, vibora, wall exits, and volley control, using repetition drills and slow-motion feedback to build cleaner mechanics. Miguel works with small groups so each participant receives individual correction rather than generic instruction, making this a strong choice for players who feel technically stuck despite regular match experience. Expect explanation of the reasoning behind each technique alongside the physical practice itself. Bring your own racket for consistency between sessions, non-marking court shoes, and a water bottle; a notebook or phone for jotting down cues is useful, since Miguel often gives cumulative feedback that builds across consecutive weeks.

name: Morning Social Drills
description: A relaxed but purposeful session for players of all levels, open to men and women aged 16 and above. Morning Social Drills at Baseline JVC blends warm-up rallies with rotating drill stations, so newer players sharpen basics while stronger players work on consistency and shot selection under gentle pressure. Yousef Halabi keeps groups moving quickly, mixing pairs each week to build court awareness and encourage social play rather than fixed partnerships. Expect volley ladders, lob-and-smash sequences, and short-form scoring games that turn technique into match-ready habits. It suits anyone wanting regular, low-stakes court time without committing to a structured course. Bring indoor court shoes, a padel racket if you own one, and water, as the twilight slot still carries warmth. Rackets can be borrowed on request. Suitable for returning players and confident beginners alike, this class runs twice weekly and welcomes drop-ins alongside regulars.

name: Tactics Workshop
description: Designed exclusively for advanced players aged 18 and over, this early morning workshop at Baseline JVC strips padel back to its tactical core. Fatima Al Zaabi leads structured analysis of court positioning, third-shot decisions, and pressure-building through the middle, using video review and live point play to reinforce concepts. Sessions focus on reading opponents' shapes, exploiting glass rebounds, and constructing points rather than simply hitting winners. Expect detailed feedback, situational drills, and competitive games where tactics are tested immediately. This class suits players already comfortable with core technique who want to close the gap between club-level and competitive play. Bring a racket you're used to competing with, non-marking court shoes, and a notebook if you like tracking patterns discussed on court. Numbers are kept small to allow individual correction. Held twice weekly before the day's heat builds, it rewards consistent attendance and honest self-assessment.

name: Adult Beginner Course
description: This beginner course at Baseline JVC introduces padel from first principles to anyone aged 16 and above, regardless of gender or prior racket sport experience. Elena Popova guides new players through grip, footwork, and the underarm serve before progressing to volleys, basic wall play, and simple scoring formats. Sessions are structured to build confidence gradually, with plenty of repetition and encouragement rather than pressure. Expect small-group drills, guided rallies, and short games that let beginners apply what they've just learned in a forgiving environment. By the end of the course, participants should be comfortable serving, sustaining a rally, and understanding basic doubles positioning. Bring a water bottle, trainers with non-marking soles, and comfortable sportswear; rackets are available to borrow for those without their own. No previous experience is required, and the pace is kept steady so nobody feels rushed. Ideal for those trying padel for the first time.

name: Adult Improver Course
description: Aimed at intermediate mixed-ability players aged 16 and above, this improver course at Baseline JVC bridges the gap between casual rallying and structured match play. Miguel Santana focuses on tightening technique already in place, refining volleys, smashes, and lob accuracy, while introducing more deliberate positioning and shot selection. Sessions include paired drills, situational point play, and light tactical coaching around when to attack the net versus defend the back wall. Participants should already be comfortable rallying and serving consistently, using this course to sharpen decision-making and consistency under mild pressure. Early sessions make the most of cooler morning air, with a brisk pace throughout. Bring a padel racket, supportive court shoes, and a towel, as the pace picks up quickly. This course suits club players wanting to move beyond beginner habits and start competing more confidently in social or ladder matches, with steady progression tracked across the weeks.

name: Ladies Beginner Academy
description: A welcoming, ladies-only introduction to padel at Baseline JVC, open to women aged 16 and above with little or no prior experience. Fatima Al Zaabi builds sessions around fundamentals: grip, stance, serving, and basic wall rebounds, delivered in a supportive, unhurried atmosphere designed to build confidence alongside skill. Participants progress through guided drills into simple rallies and beginner-friendly games, learning core positioning for doubles play along the way. The evening slot suits those balancing work or family commitments, offering a sociable end to the week alongside like-minded newcomers. Expect plenty of repetition, clear technical correction, and encouragement to ask questions freely. Bring comfortable sportswear, non-marking court shoes, and water; rackets are available to borrow for anyone without their own. No previous racket sport background is needed, and the emphasis throughout stays on enjoyment and steady improvement rather than competition, making this an ideal entry point for women new to the game.

name: Ladies Social Doubles
description: This ladies-only class at Baseline JVC suits intermediate players aged 18 and above who already rally confidently and want regular, social match play with a coaching edge. Fatima Al Zaabi structures sessions around doubles positioning, communication between partners, and shot selection during live points, rotating pairings so participants play alongside a variety of partners each week. Expect warm-up drills followed by extended game play, with Fatima offering feedback between sets rather than constant interruption, keeping the tone competitive but relaxed. Participants should already understand basic scoring and serving; this class builds on that foundation to sharpen tactical awareness within a doubles format. It's a popular fixture for women wanting consistent evening court time in good company. Bring a racket, comfortable indoor-appropriate footwear, and water, as sessions run at a steady pace across ninety minutes. Ideal for those looking to combine social connection with genuine on-court improvement.

name: Adult Beginner Course
description: Held at Baseline Yas Island, this beginner course welcomes men and women aged 16 and above who are new to padel or returning after a long break. Reem Darwish covers the essentials: grip, footwork, serving technique, and basic wall play, before introducing simple rallies and beginner scoring formats. Sessions are paced to let participants absorb one skill before layering on the next, with plenty of repetition and encouraging feedback throughout. By the end of the course, players should feel comfortable serving reliably, sustaining short rallies, and understanding basic doubles positioning on court. Bring trainers with non-marking soles, comfortable sportswear, and a water bottle; rackets can be borrowed for those without their own. No prior racket sport experience is necessary, and the relaxed evening slot suits those coming straight from work. This course is a solid starting point for anyone wanting a genuine foundation in padel fundamentals.

name: Adult Improver Course
description: This improver course at Baseline Yas Island is built for mixed intermediate players aged 16 and above who already rally and serve with some consistency. Ahmed Sultan sharpens technique across volleys, smashes, and lob placement, while introducing tactical concepts like court positioning and shot selection during live points. Sessions combine paired drills with situational game play, gradually increasing pressure so participants learn to execute under match-like conditions. The evening timeslot suits those finishing work commitments, with a brisk pace that keeps energy high despite the hour. Expect constructive feedback after each drill and structured progression across the course rather than one-off tips. Bring a padel racket, supportive court shoes, and a towel, as sessions build in intensity toward the end. Ideal for club players ready to move beyond beginner habits, this course helps bridge the gap toward confident, competitive social play.

name: Ladies Beginner Academy
description: This ladies-only programme at Baseline Yas Island welcomes women aged sixteen and over who are picking up a racket for the first time. Chiara Rossi leads sessions twice weekly, on Wednesday and Saturday mornings, focusing on the fundamentals that make padel so addictive: grip, the underarm serve, wall rebounds and basic court positioning. Drills are kept light-hearted and social, with plenty of rotation so everyone plays with different partners and builds confidence at their own pace. Over successive weeks the group progresses from simple rallying to constructing short points, learning when to move up to the net and how to defend from the back wall. It's an encouraging environment for beginners who want technical grounding without pressure. Bring comfortable sportswear, padel or tennis trainers with non-marking soles, a water bottle and, if you own one, your own racket, though loaner racquets are available for newcomers still deciding on their game.

name: Ladies Social Doubles
description: Held on Saturday evenings at Baseline Yas Island, this ladies-only session suits intermediate players aged eighteen and over who already understand the basics and want to sharpen doubles play in a relaxed, social format. Noor Al Hashimi organises matches and rotating pairings so participants face a variety of styles across the ninety-minute session, with light coaching input on shot selection, communication with a partner and exploiting angles off the glass. Expect warm-up rallies followed by mostly match-based play, with Noor stepping in between games to flag tactical improvements. It's less a technical clinic and more a chance to build court awareness while enjoying competitive, friendly matches. Regular attendees often form lasting playing partnerships here. Bring padel shoes, comfortable activewear suited to the evening heat, a racket if you have one, and a water bottle, as the pace stays lively throughout and courtside breaks are brief between rotations.

name: Junior Academy
description: Junior Academy runs on Wednesday and Saturday evenings at Baseline Yas Island for mixed groups of boys and girls aged nine to fifteen who are new to padel. Bilal Chaudhry introduces the sport through games-based drills that build hand-eye coordination, basic swing mechanics and an understanding of the smaller, walled court before layering in serving technique and simple rally patterns. Sessions balance structured coaching with plenty of fun, competitive mini-games to keep younger participants engaged throughout the ninety minutes. Players leave each session with a clearer grasp of scoring, court etiquette and the teamwork doubles demands. It suits complete beginners as well as juniors with some racket-sport background looking to transition into padel specifically. Bring trainers suitable for court use, comfortable kit, a water bottle and sun protection for the walk to and from courts. Rackets are available to borrow, though juniors with their own are welcome to bring them along.

name: Junior Performance Squad
description: Junior Performance Squad meets Sunday and Tuesday evenings at Baseline Yas Island for mixed juniors aged twelve to seventeen who already play at an intermediate level and want a more demanding programme. Bilal Chaudhry structures sessions around match-specific scenarios, sharpening volleys, smashes and lob defence while introducing tactical concepts like court coverage and shot selection under pressure. Fitness elements are woven into drills to build the movement and reaction speed padel at this level demands. Video feedback and point analysis feature periodically, helping players understand patterns in their own game and their opponents'. This squad suits juniors aiming to compete in tournaments or simply push their standard higher within a focused peer group. Bring padel shoes, training kit appropriate for high-intensity movement, a water bottle and a personal racket if owned. Consistent attendance is encouraged, as sessions build progressively on skills and partnerships developed across the week.

name: Kids Padel Starters
description: Kids Padel Starters takes place on Wednesday and Saturday mornings at Baseline Yas Island, designed specifically for mixed groups of children aged five to eight taking their very first steps on court. Bilal Chaudhry uses playful, game-led activities rather than formal drills to introduce balance, basic hand-eye coordination and gentle familiarity with a lightweight racket and soft balls suited to small hands. The focus stays firmly on enjoyment and movement, with short attention-friendly activities that build toward simple rallying by the end of a term. Parents can expect their children to come away with growing confidence, better coordination and an early love of racket sports in a safe, encouraging setting. Bring comfortable sports clothing, trainers with good grip, a labelled water bottle and a sun hat, as part of the session may take place in shaded outdoor areas. Rackets are provided, so no equipment purchase is necessary to begin.

name: Cardio Padel
description: Cardio Padel runs Monday and Wednesday evenings at Baseline Yas Island and is open to all levels, mixed, for players aged sixteen and over who want a fitness-forward take on the sport. Chiara Rossi structures the ninety minutes around continuous movement, combining padel-specific drills with interval-style footwork patterns, quick reflex exercises and high-repetition rallying to elevate heart rate throughout. Technical coaching still features, but the emphasis leans toward conditioning, agility and stamina rather than deep tactical work, making it approachable whether you're a first-timer or an experienced player after a harder workout. Expect to leave sweaty, energised and with sharper footwork on court. Because all levels train together, drills are adaptable in intensity so nobody feels out of place. Bring supportive trainers, breathable activewear, a towel and a generously filled water bottle, since the pace rarely slows and hydration breaks are kept brief between exercises.

name: Competition Squad
description: Competition Squad, held Tuesday and Thursday evenings at Baseline Yas Island, is built for advanced mixed players aged sixteen and over preparing for tournament-level padel. Pablo Ortega drives sessions with high-intensity match play, situational drills replicating competitive scenarios, and detailed work on advanced shots such as bandejas, viboras and precise smashes off the back wall. Tactical discussion covers court positioning, reading opponents and closing out tight points, with Pablo offering direct feedback throughout. This squad expects players to arrive already comfortable with doubles strategy and consistent shot execution, as sessions move quickly and assume a solid technical base. Fitness demands are considerable, given the match-intensity format across ninety minutes. It suits players actively competing or aiming to enter tournaments soon. Bring performance padel shoes, a spare shirt, a well-stocked water bottle and a personal racket, since equipment familiarity matters at this level and loaner rackets may not suit advanced play styles.

name: Technique Clinic
description: Technique Clinic runs early on Saturday and Monday mornings at Baseline Yas Island, aimed at mixed intermediate players aged sixteen and over who want focused, detail-oriented coaching rather than full match play. Lucas Benitez breaks sessions into targeted blocks covering serve consistency, volley technique, smash accuracy and wall-rebound control, using repetition drills and small-sided practice to isolate and correct specific habits. Rather than broad tactical themes, the clinic drills down into the mechanics behind reliable shot-making, helping participants understand why certain strokes break down under pressure. Expect individual feedback throughout, as group sizes are kept manageable for hands-on correction. It suits players who already rally competently but want cleaner technique before pushing into more competitive formats. Bring padel shoes, comfortable morning kit suited to the cooler start, a water bottle and your own racket if possible, since fine-tuning grip and swing benefits from familiarity with one's regular equipment.

name: Morning Social Drills
description: Morning Social Drills brings together players of every standard at Baseline Yas Island for a relaxed but purposeful hour and a half on court. Open to mixed groups aged sixteen and above, the session is built around rotating drill stations that sharpen volleys, lobs and wall-play before finishing with points-based games that mix the group up each week. Coach Reem Darwish keeps the pace friendly and inclusive, offering pointers as needed rather than running a strict lesson plan, which makes this a popular way to end the working week. Newer players pick up positioning habits by playing alongside more experienced regulars, while established players get extra reps and social match play without the pressure of a formal course. Bring court shoes with non-marking soles, a padel racket if you own one, and a bottle of water. Loan rackets are available on request. No partner or fixed group is required; simply arrive and you will be placed into a group on the day.

name: Tactics Workshop
description: Tactics Workshop at Baseline Yas Island is built for advanced players who already have solid technique and want to sharpen the thinking behind their game. Open to mixed groups aged eighteen and above, sessions run twice weekly in the evening and focus on match strategy rather than repetitive drilling. Expect detailed work on positioning, court coverage, shot selection under pressure, and reading an opponent's patterns before they commit to a play. Coaches break down real match scenarios, walk through when to lob versus when to press the net, and refine communication between pairs so decisions happen faster and with less hesitation. Video review may feature occasionally to highlight recurring habits worth adjusting. This class suits competitive club players and those preparing for tournament play rather than newcomers. Bring your own racket, indoor court shoes, and a full water bottle, as pace is high and rest breaks are brief. Small group sizes keep feedback personal and specific throughout.

name: Adult Beginner Course
description: This Adult Beginner Course at Baseline Yas Island is built for anyone stepping onto a padel court for the first time, whether you have a racquet-sports background or none at all. Open to mixed groups of adults aged 16 and above, with no upper age limit, sessions run twice weekly on Tuesday and Thursday evenings from 19:00 to 20:30. Coaches focus on the fundamentals: grip, footwork, the underarm serve, and reading the glass and mesh walls that make padel distinct from tennis. Expect a warm-up, technical drills in small groups, and plenty of supervised rally play so new habits stick before points count. By the end of the course, participants should serve reliably, sustain a rally, and understand basic scoring and court positioning for doubles play. Bring court shoes with non-marking soles, comfortable sports clothing suited to the evening warmth, and a water bottle. Racquets are available to borrow, though players with their own are welcome to bring them.

name: Adult Improver Course
description: Baseline Yas Island's Adult Improver Course is built for mixed-gender players aged sixteen and up who already have a handful of matches under their belt and want to move beyond basics. Sessions on Saturdays and Mondays, 17:30 to 19:00, focus on the details that separate improvers from intermediates: consistent volleys at the net, smarter positioning as a pair, and reading when to attack the glass versus reset the point. Coaches break the ninety minutes into a warm-up, technical drilling on shot selection and bandeja control, then live points where new patterns get tested under pressure. Expect honest feedback on footwork and court coverage, plus tactical chat on communication with your partner. It suits players comfortable with rallying who now want structure and match-craft rather than pure fundamentals. Bring court shoes with non-marking soles, a padel racquet if you own one, and a bottle of water. Balls and loaner racquets are available on request. Numbers are kept small so everyone gets proper court time each week.

name: Ladies Beginner Academy
description: Ladies Beginner Academy at Baseline Yas Island is a relaxed, supportive introduction to padel for women aged 16 and over, with no upper age limit and no prior racket sports experience required. Sessions run twice weekly on Saturdays and Mondays from 09:00 to 10:30, giving newcomers plenty of time to settle into the rhythm of the game. Each class opens with a guided warm-up before moving into core fundamentals: grip, footwork, the underarm serve, and controlled volleys at the net. Coaches break down positioning and court awareness using simple drills and plenty of repetition, so confidence builds steadily week to week. Group sizes are kept small and entirely female, creating a comfortable environment for first-timers to ask questions and progress at their own pace. By the end of the course, participants should be comfortable rallying, serving, and understanding basic scoring and doubles strategy. Bring court shoes with non-marking soles, comfortable activewear, a water bottle, and a padel racket if you own one; loan rackets are available on request.

name: Ladies Social Doubles
description: Ladies Social Doubles at Baseline Yas Island brings together women who already understand the basics of padel and want to sharpen their game in a relaxed, competitive environment. Open to players aged 18 and above, this session is exclusively for women and runs twice weekly, giving regulars a chance to build familiarity with court rotations and playing partners. Each ninety-minute class begins with a warm-up and light drilling to reinforce intermediate skills such as volleys, lobs and wall play, before moving into rotating doubles matches guided by a coach who offers feedback between games. Expect plenty of movement, tactical pointers on positioning, and a genuinely social atmosphere where friendships form as quickly as good habits. It suits players comfortable with rallying and scoring who want match practice rather than beginner instruction. Bring court shoes with non-marking soles, a padel racquet if you own one, water, and a light layer for the changeover between sets.

name: Junior Academy
description: Junior Academy at Baseline Yas Island is a mixed-gender programme for young players aged nine to fifteen who are new to padel or still finding their feet on court. Sessions run twice weekly, giving juniors a chance to build real consistency without it feeling like a chore. Each class opens with movement and racket-familiarisation drills before progressing into grip, the forehand and backhand, and an introduction to reading the ball off the glass. Coaches keep groups small and energetic, mixing structured repetition with point-play so technique translates into match situations. Beyond strokes, juniors pick up court positioning, basic scoring, and the sort of communication skills that make doubles enjoyable rather than chaotic. It's a supportive environment where mistakes are treated as part of learning, and confidence tends to build quickly. Participants should bring a padel or tennis racket if they own one, indoor court shoes, a refillable water bottle, and sun protection, since some drills spill onto the outer practice courts. All equipment can be borrowed if needed.

name: Junior Performance Squad
description: Junior Performance Squad is a fast-paced session for young players aged 12 to 17 who already have solid padel fundamentals and want to sharpen their competitive edge. Open to boys and girls, the group trains together and focuses on the tactical side of the game: shot selection, court positioning, and reading an opponent's pattern of play. Each Friday evening session at Baseline Yas Island opens with a dynamic warm-up before moving into drills that build consistency off the back wall, then progresses into live points where the coaching team calls out scenarios to test decision-making under pressure. Expect plenty of net play work and doubles communication practice, since this age group is pushed towards match-ready habits rather than isolated technique. Participants should bring their own racket, indoor court shoes, and a refillable water bottle; balls and bibs are provided. Ideal for juniors already competing locally or those preparing to step into their first tournaments, this squad builds both game intelligence and the resilience needed for closer matches.

name: Adult Beginner Course
description: This course is the natural starting point for adults who are new to padel and want a structured route into the game. Open to all adults aged 16 and over, in a mixed group, sessions run twice weekly at Baseline Khalifa City under the guidance of Aisha Al Marri. Across the course you'll build the fundamentals: grip, the underarm serve, forehand and backhand basics, reading the glass and wire, and simple positioning as a pair. Aisha keeps drills light and social, so nerves settle quickly and rallies start appearing within the first few sessions. Expect plenty of repetition-based practice, short-sided games, and clear feedback on technique. It suits anyone arriving with no racket-sport background as well as those returning to sport after a break. Bring a padel or tennis racket if you own one (loan rackets are available), non-marking court shoes, water, and light indoor-friendly kit, since the evening slot can still feel warm.

name: Adult Improver Course
description: Designed for players who already have a handful of matches under their belt, this intermediate course sharpens the details that separate steady rallies from controlled points. Open to mixed adults aged 16 and above, sessions take place twice a week at Baseline Khalifa City with coach Ravi Menon. Expect focused work on smash and bandeja technique, using the walls with intent, court positioning as a pair, and smarter shot selection under pressure. Ravi structures each session around a technical block followed by point-play, so improvements get tested in realistic scenarios straight away. It's aimed at players comfortable with the basic strokes and scoring who want to move beyond social rallies into more competitive doubles. Expect honest, specific feedback and a group of similarly progressing players around you. Bring your own racket, comfortable indoor or non-marking court shoes, and a bottle of water, as the pace here is noticeably brisker than beginner level.

name: Ladies Beginner Academy
description: A relaxed, ladies-only introduction to padel held in the early morning quiet at Baseline Khalifa City, this academy is built for women aged 16 and over taking their first steps on court. Coach Aisha Al Marri leads small, supportive groups through the essentials: racket control, the serve, basic rallying, and simple doubles positioning, all explained without assuming any prior experience. The tone is encouraging rather than competitive, with plenty of repetition so techniques genuinely settle in before pace is added. Many who join have never picked up a racket before, while others are returning to sport and want a comfortable space to rebuild confidence. Sessions blend short technical drills with light-hearted mini games, so friendships tend to form quickly among the group. Bring a racket if you have one, though loan equipment is available, along with non-marking court shoes, water, and a light layer for the cooler start to the day.

name: Ladies Social Doubles
description: This ladies-only session is built around match play rather than formal drilling, giving intermediate players a regular evening slot to sharpen their doubles game at Baseline Khalifa City. Open to women aged 18 and over, it runs twice weekly under the eye of Aisha Al Marri, who rotates pairings, sets scoring formats, and steps in with tactical pointers between games rather than lengthy technical breakdowns. Participants should already be comfortable with serving, basic wall play, and scoring, as the focus here is on decision-making, communication with a partner, and consistency under match conditions. It's a popular fixture for women who want competitive rallies in a friendly, low-pressure atmosphere, and a good way to meet regular playing partners. Expect a fast-moving evening of short matches with brief coaching interludes. Bring your own racket, non-marking court shoes, and water, and arrive ready to play, since games begin promptly once the group is warmed up.

name: Junior Academy
description: A lively introduction to padel for younger players, this academy at Baseline Khalifa City is designed for boys and girls aged 9 to 15 taking their first proper steps into the sport. Coach Marwan Haddad runs mixed sessions twice a week, blending fun, game-based learning with the core technical building blocks: grip, basic strokes, serving, and simple court awareness. Sessions are paced to hold young attention, moving between short drills, mini challenges, and supervised rally practice, so skills develop naturally through play rather than repetition alone. It suits complete beginners as well as juniors with some casual experience who want proper coaching structure. Marwan places emphasis on coordination, confidence, and good court habits early on, setting a solid foundation for further progression. Bring a junior or adult racket sized appropriately for the child if available, non-marking court shoes, a water bottle, and a cap or light layer for comfort during the session.

name: Junior Performance Squad
description: This squad is aimed at junior players aged 12 to 17 who already have solid padel fundamentals and are ready to train with greater intensity. Held twice weekly at Baseline Khalifa City under coach Ravi Menon, sessions mix mixed-gender groups and focus on intermediate-level technical refinement: smash and volley precision, tactical positioning, footwork patterns, and match-style decision-making. Ravi structures training around progressive drills that build in speed and complexity, followed by competitive point play where juniors apply what they've practised. It's suited to players already comfortable with rallying, serving, and basic doubles tactics who are looking to move towards more structured, competitive padel. Expect a disciplined but encouraging environment, with attention given to both technical detail and match temperament. Bring your own racket, non-marking court shoes, a water bottle, and suitable sports kit, as sessions are physically demanding and run at a noticeably higher tempo than entry-level junior classes.

name: Kids Padel Starters
description: A gentle, playful first encounter with padel for the youngest players, this programme at Baseline Khalifa City welcomes children aged 5 to 8 in a mixed group setting. Coach Ravi Menon leads sessions twice a week, using games, coordination exercises, and simplified rallying to introduce racket and ball skills in a way that keeps young children engaged throughout. Rather than formal technique from the outset, the emphasis is on movement, hand-eye coordination, and basic understanding of the court and ball, with proper strokes introduced gradually as confidence grows. It's an ideal starting point for children with no prior racket-sport experience, and parents are welcome to watch from the side. Expect lots of variety within each session to match shorter attention spans. Bring a lightweight junior racket if the family owns one, though club equipment is provided, along with named water bottles, sun protection, and comfortable trainers suitable for court surfaces.

name: Cardio Padel
description: Part fitness class, part padel session, Cardio Padel at Baseline Khalifa City is built for adults of any playing standard who want an energetic workout alongside their court time. Open to mixed players aged 16 and over, sessions run twice weekly with coach Marta Vidal, who combines fast-paced drills, footwork circuits, and continuous rally sequences designed to keep heart rates elevated throughout. Rather than isolated technical coaching, the focus is on movement efficiency, reaction speed, and sustained activity, with padel skills reinforced naturally through repetition under fatigue. It suits complete beginners looking for an active introduction to the sport as well as experienced players after a high-intensity supplement to regular matches. Marta adjusts intensity across the group, so mixed abilities train comfortably side by side. Bring a racket if you have one, indoor-appropriate non-marking shoes, a good supply of water, and a towel, since this session is noticeably more physically demanding than a standard class.

name: Competition Squad
description: Competition Squad is the advanced training block for players at Baseline Khalifa City who are already competing or preparing to enter tournaments. Open to mixed groups aged 16 and over, sessions run on Saturday and Monday evenings under Salem Al Ketbi, who structures each two-part block around match simulation, pressure drills and detailed feedback on shot selection. Expect fast-paced points, live scoring scenarios, and work on smash defence, lob precision and net transitions against strong opposition. Salem also spends time on match temperament, reviewing decision-making under fatigue and how to close out tight sets. This programme suits players with solid technical foundations who want consistent, high-intensity court time rather than instruction from scratch. Bring indoor and outdoor appropriate padel shoes, a racket you already compete with, water for a long session, and a willingness to be paired against unfamiliar partners. Places are limited to keep the standard high and the pace honest.

name: Technique Clinic
description: Technique Clinic is an intermediate-level session at Baseline Khalifa City focused purely on stroke mechanics rather than match play. Coached by Marwan Haddad on Sunday and Tuesday evenings, the class is mixed and open to anyone aged 16 and above who already understands basic rules and rallying but wants cleaner, more repeatable technique. Each session breaks down a specific element, such as the bandeja, vibora, or wall rebound control, with slow-speed repetition before adding pace and pressure. Marwan works in small groups so every player gets individual correction on grip, contact point and footwork patterns. Participants leave with a clearer understanding of why certain shots fail under match conditions and how to adjust in real time. This is a good fit for club-level players plateauing on technique rather than fitness. Bring a racket, non-marking court shoes, and a notebook or phone if you like recording drill sequences for practice between sessions.

name: Morning Social Drills
description: Morning Social Drills is an easy-going, all-levels session at Baseline Khalifa City designed to get players moving before the day heats up. Held Wednesday and Saturday mornings with Marwan Haddad, the class is mixed and open to anyone aged 16 and over, from complete beginners to established club players looking for a relaxed hit. The format rotates through short drill stations covering serving, volleys and rally consistency, followed by informal doubles points so everyone gets varied court time and partners. Marwan keeps instruction light-touch, offering pointers where useful but prioritising movement, rhythm and enjoyment over intensive correction. It works well as a low-pressure way to build match minutes, meet other members, or simply stay sharp between more serious training blocks. Bring a racket if you own one, light indoor-suitable trainers, and a refillable water bottle, since sessions run at a steady pace across the full ninety minutes. Rackets are available to borrow on request.

name: Tactics Workshop
description: Tactics Workshop is an advanced, tactics-focused session at Baseline Khalifa City for adult players aged 18 and over who already have the strokes and want to sharpen decision-making. Running Wednesday and Saturday mornings straight after Morning Social Drills, the class is mixed and led by Salem Al Ketbi, who sets up realistic point scenarios to work through positioning, court coverage and shot selection as a pair. Expect detailed breakdowns of when to lob, when to attack the net, and how to read an opponent's weaker side, with video-style walkthroughs on court rather than lengthy lectures. Players rotate partners regularly so everyone experiences different playing styles and communication demands. This session suits competitive players who want to understand the game beneath the shots rather than repeat technical drilling. Bring a racket, suitable indoor court shoes, and water, along with a partner mindset ready for feedback mid-point rather than only between games.

name: Adult Beginner Course
description: Adult Beginner Course at Baseline Khalifa City is a structured introduction to padel for anyone aged 16 and over who has never picked up a racket or played only a handful of times. Running Sunday and Thursday evenings with Marwan Haddad, the mixed class covers the fundamentals in a logical order: grip and stance, forehand and backhand groundstrokes, serving rules, and the basics of using the glass and mesh walls. Marwan keeps group sizes manageable so beginners get hands-on correction rather than getting lost in a crowd, and each session ends with light, supervised points to apply what has just been learned. By the end of the course participants should understand scoring, court positioning and the etiquette of doubles play. No previous racket sport experience is required. Bring comfortable indoor-suitable trainers, water, and a racket if you have one, though loan equipment is available for those just starting out.

name: Adult Improver Course
description: Adult Improver Course is designed for players at Baseline Khalifa City who have completed beginner training and can sustain a rally but want more structure before progressing further. Coached by Ravi Menon on Tuesday and Thursday mornings, the mixed session is open to adults aged 16 and over and focuses on consolidating consistency across all four walls, improving serve placement, and introducing early net play and simple attacking shots. Ravi builds each class around a progression, starting with controlled drilling and moving into semi-competitive points where players are encouraged to apply the shot just practised. Communication with a doubles partner and basic court positioning are also covered in detail. This course suits players who want fewer unforced errors and a better read of when to defend versus attack. Bring a racket, indoor-appropriate footwear, and water, and expect a fair amount of repetition as movement patterns become more automatic through the weeks.

name: Ladies Beginner Academy
description: Ladies Beginner Academy is a women-only introduction to padel at Baseline Khalifa City, welcoming participants aged 16 and over regardless of prior racket sport experience. Held Sunday and Thursday mornings, the course is led by Aisha Al Marri in a supportive, unhurried environment aimed at building confidence alongside technique. Sessions cover grip, footwork, forehand and backhand basics, serving, and an introduction to using the surrounding walls, with plenty of repetition to embed each skill before moving on. Aisha places particular emphasis on communication between doubles partners and reading the court, so participants finish the course comfortable playing a full social match. The atmosphere is deliberately relaxed, making it a popular option for those who feel self-conscious starting a new sport in mixed groups. Bring comfortable indoor court shoes, water, and a racket if available, though the club can provide loan equipment for the full duration of the course while beginners decide on their own kit.

name: Adult Beginner Course
description: Adult Beginner Course at Baseline Al Ain introduces padel from first principles for anyone aged 16 and over with little or no previous experience. Running as a single weekly session on Friday evenings, the mixed class is coached by Ibrahim Saleh, who structures the ninety minutes around grip, basic groundstrokes, serving rules and an introduction to playing the ball off the glass and mesh walls. Small group sizes mean each participant receives regular individual correction rather than generic instruction, and Ibrahim closes most sessions with light supervised points so new skills are tested in a realistic setting straight away. Over the course of the programme, players should develop a working understanding of scoring, positioning in doubles, and basic on-court etiquette. This is an ideal starting point for anyone new to racket sports or returning after a long break. Bring indoor-suitable trainers and water, with loan rackets available for those who haven't yet bought their own.

name: Adult Improver Course
description: This intermediate course at Baseline Al Ain is designed for mixed groups of adult players aged sixteen and above who already have the basics in hand and want to sharpen their game. Under the guidance of Ibrahim Saleh, sessions running on Saturday and Monday mornings focus on consistency from the back court, volley technique at the net, and reading the glass to build smarter shot selection. Expect structured drills, point-play scenarios, and tactical feedback aimed at reducing unforced errors and improving positioning as a pair. It suits players who can sustain a rally and are ready to add variety, spin, and court craft to their toolkit. Bring your own racket, indoor court shoes with non-marking soles, and a bottle of water, as courts can warm up quickly even early in the day. A light towel is recommended. No prior competitive experience is necessary, just a willingness to train with intent.

name: Ladies Beginner Academy
description: A welcoming introduction to padel for women aged sixteen and over who are new to the sport, this ladies-only academy at Baseline Al Ain runs on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons under coach Mariam Al Ameri. Sessions cover the fundamentals: grip, footwork, serving, and understanding how the walls come into play, all taught in a relaxed and supportive environment. Participants will build confidence in basic rallying, learn simple positioning as a doubles team, and start to understand scoring and court etiquette. It is an ideal starting point for anyone curious about the sport but nervous about jumping into mixed sessions. Please bring a racket if you own one, though loan equipment is available on request, along with comfortable sportswear and flat, non-marking court shoes. Water and a small towel are recommended, as the pace picks up once the basics click. No previous racket sports experience is required.

name: Ladies Social Doubles
description: Held on Friday evenings at Baseline Al Ain, this ladies-only session is aimed at intermediate players aged eighteen and above who want to play regularly in a friendly, low-pressure format. Coached by Mariam Al Ameri, the ninety-minute sessions blend light technical pointers with plenty of match play, rotating partners so participants build variety in their doubles understanding. Expect coaching on communication at the net, shot selection under pressure, and tactical positioning during rallies, all wrapped around genuine game time rather than isolated drills. It suits those who already have a working rally and serve and are looking to sharpen decision-making while enjoying the social side of the sport. Bring your own racket, indoor-appropriate footwear with non-marking soles, and water, as the pace stays lively throughout. It is a popular way to close out the week, combining exercise, competition, and company in equal measure.

name: Junior Academy
description: This beginner programme at Baseline Al Ain introduces padel to children aged nine to fifteen in a mixed group setting, running on Sunday and Thursday early evenings under coach Mariam Al Ameri. Sessions are built around fun, movement-based games that teach grip, basic swing mechanics, and how to use the court walls, alongside simple rules and scoring. Coaches focus on hand-eye coordination, safe movement around the court, and early rallying skills, gradually introducing serving and basic doubles positioning as confidence grows. It is an ideal entry point for young players with little or no racket sports background, encouraging teamwork and enjoyment as much as technique. Participants should bring their own racket if available, though club equipment can be arranged in advance, plus comfortable sports clothing, non-marking court shoes, and a water bottle. Sun protection is advised for early sessions. Parents are welcome to observe from the seating areas pitchside.

name: Junior Performance Squad
description: Designed for young players aged twelve to seventeen who already have a solid grasp of padel basics, this intermediate squad at Baseline Al Ain trains on Wednesday and Saturday evenings under coach Mariam Al Ameri. The mixed group sessions raise the intensity with structured drills on shot consistency, net play, lob and smash technique, and tactical awareness in doubles formation. Coaching emphasises match-specific scenarios, helping juniors translate practice patterns into real point-winning decisions, with an eye toward those considering more competitive play in future. It suits committed young players ready to train with focus and take feedback on technique and footwork. Participants should bring their own racket, suitable indoor court shoes with non-marking soles, and a water bottle, as sessions run at a good pace across ninety minutes. A light snack afterward is often welcome given the later finish time. Consistent attendance is encouraged to track progress.

name: Kids Padel Starters
description: A gentle, playful first step into padel for children aged five to eight, this mixed beginner session at Baseline Al Ain runs on Friday afternoons under coach Hamad Al Dhaheri. Using scaled-down games, simple targets, and lots of movement, sessions introduce basic racket handling, hand-eye coordination, and an early feel for hitting a ball over a net, all without the pressure of formal rules. Children will learn to hold a racket correctly, track a bouncing ball, and take their first swings in a safe, encouraging setting designed around short attention spans and high energy. Small rackets are provided for those who do not yet have their own, though families are welcome to bring a suitably sized one. Comfortable clothing, closed-toe sports shoes, and a water bottle are recommended. Parents can watch from the sideline seating, and sessions are kept light-hearted throughout to build enthusiasm for the sport early on.

name: Cardio Padel
description: Open to all levels and all adults aged sixteen and above, this mixed cardio-focused session at Baseline Al Ain runs on Sunday and Thursday mornings under coach Hamad Al Dhaheri. Rather than isolated technique work, the format keeps players moving continuously through fast-paced drills, rotating rallies, and fitness-driven exercises designed to raise the heart rate while still sharpening padel-specific movement and reflexes. Participants will improve court coverage, reaction speed, and general conditioning, all while picking up incidental technical polish along the way. It suits both newcomers looking for an active, low-pressure introduction to the sport and established players wanting a fitness-oriented session to complement their regular training. Bring a racket if you have one, along with proper court shoes with non-marking soles, a water bottle, and a towel, as this session is noticeably more physical than a standard technical class. Suitable for a broad range of fitness levels.

name: Competition Squad
description: This advanced squad at Baseline Al Ain is built for experienced mixed adult players aged sixteen and above who compete or intend to compete regularly, training on Friday early evenings under coach Hamad Al Dhaheri. Sessions combine high-intensity drilling with match simulation, covering advanced net exchanges, defensive lobbing, bandeja and vibora technique, and the fine details of doubles tactics under pressure. Coaching is geared toward refining shot precision, anticipation, and mental resilience in competitive situations, with regular feedback on positioning and shot selection during live points. It suits players with strong existing technique who are looking to compete at club tournaments or higher, rather than those still building fundamentals. Bring your own racket, appropriate indoor court shoes with non-marking soles, and water, as sessions are demanding across the full ninety minutes. Prior experience playing competitive matches is recommended before joining this group.

name: Technique Clinic
description: Technique Clinic at Baseline Al Ain is built for intermediate players, open to both men and women aged 16 and above, who want to sharpen the finer points of their game rather than simply rally for fun. Running twice weekly on Wednesday and Saturday evenings from 19:00 to 20:30, sessions are coached by Gonzalo Ferrer and focus on wall play, volley control, bandeja technique and shot selection under match-like pressure. Expect drills broken into small groups, video-style feedback from the coach, and plenty of repetition designed to turn theory into muscle memory. Participants should already be comfortable with basic rallying and scoring, as the pace assumes some court experience. Bring your own racket if you have one, indoor or non-marking court shoes, and a water bottle, as sessions run at a high tempo with limited rest between drills. Bibs and balls are provided for every clinic.

name: Adult Beginner Course
description: Adult Beginner Course at Baseline Al Majaz is a friendly, mixed-gender introduction to padel for absolute newcomers aged 16 and over. Held on Saturday evenings from 19:00 to 20:30 and led by Amina Belhaj, the course walks participants through grip, serve, basic scoring and how to use the glass and mesh walls to their advantage. Sessions are structured around short explanations followed by lots of hands-on practice, so nervous first-timers quickly feel comfortable on court alongside others at the same stage. By the end of the course, players will understand rally basics, positioning as part of a doubles pair, and simple court etiquette. No previous racket sports experience is required, and rackets are available to borrow for the first few sessions. Participants should bring flat, non-marking court shoes, comfortable sportswear and water. It is an easygoing, social starting point for anyone curious about the game.

name: Ladies Adult Improver Course
description: Ladies Adult Improver Course at Baseline Al Majaz is designed for women aged 16 and above who already have basic rallying experience and want to move confidently into intermediate play. Taking place on Saturday evenings from 20:30 to 22:00 under coach Carlos Ibanez, the course develops consistency off the walls, smarter shot selection and early tactical awareness for doubles positioning. Sessions combine structured drills with supervised points play, giving participants a chance to apply new skills in realistic match situations. Expect focused work on lobs, smashes and defensive recovery, alongside guidance on communication with a playing partner. This course suits those who have completed a beginner programme or played casually for some time. Bring your own racket where possible, non-marking court shoes and water, as the pace is quicker than introductory sessions. It is a supportive, ladies-only environment for building real match confidence.

name: Ladies Beginner Academy
description: Ladies Beginner Academy at Baseline Al Majaz offers women aged 16 and over a relaxed, ladies-only route into padel from complete scratch. Running Saturday mornings from 09:00 to 10:30 with coach Amina Belhaj, sessions cover grip, footwork, serving and the basics of using the court walls, all taught at a gentle, encouraging pace. Small group sizes mean plenty of individual attention, and the atmosphere is designed to feel welcoming for anyone who has never picked up a padel racket before. Participants will leave understanding simple scoring, basic rally patterns and how to move safely around a doubles court. No experience or existing equipment is necessary, as loan rackets are available on request. Attendees should wear comfortable sportswear and non-marking court shoes, and bring water for the session. It is an ideal starting point for women looking to build confidence in a supportive, all-female setting before progressing further.

name: Ladies Social Doubles
description: Ladies Social Doubles at Baseline Al Majaz is a semi-structured session for women aged 18 and above who already play at an intermediate level and want regular, enjoyable match practice. Held Wednesday and Saturday evenings from 19:00 to 20:30 under the guidance of Noura Al Suwaidi, the format blends light coaching input with rotated doubles matches, so players sharpen tactics while enjoying genuine competitive points. Expect feedback on shot selection, court positioning and communication between partners, delivered informally between games rather than through isolated drills. It is a popular option for those who have finished improver-level coaching and want a consistent group to play with each week. Participants should bring their own racket, non-marking court shoes and water, as the emphasis is on playing time rather than repetitive drilling. The relaxed, ladies-only atmosphere makes it easy to meet regular playing partners of a similar standard.

name: Ladies Junior Academy
description: Ladies Junior Academy at Baseline Al Majaz introduces girls aged 9 to 15 to padel in a supportive, all-female group setting. Sessions run Saturday mornings from 09:00 to 10:30 under coach Zayed Al Nuaimi, covering the fundamentals of grip, footwork, serving and basic rallying through games-based drills designed to keep younger players engaged. The focus is on building coordination, court awareness and confidence rather than intense competition, with plenty of encouragement for those trying padel for the very first time. By progressing through the academy, participants will learn simple scoring, how to work with a doubles partner, and safe movement around the court. No prior experience is needed, and junior-sized rackets are available for those without their own. Participants should wear comfortable sportswear, non-marking court shoes and bring a water bottle. It is a positive first step for young girls looking to enjoy padel socially while developing real technical foundations.

name: Ladies Junior Performance Squad
description: Ladies Junior Performance Squad at Baseline Al Majaz is an intermediate-level programme for girls aged 12 to 17 who already have solid padel fundamentals and are looking to progress towards more competitive play. Sessions take place Friday mornings from 09:00 to 10:30 under coach Zayed Al Nuaimi, with training built around tactical doubles positioning, consistency off the walls, and sharper shot execution under game pressure. Squad members work through structured drills followed by supervised match play, allowing coaches to give targeted feedback on decision-making and movement patterns. This programme suits juniors who have completed a beginner academy or have equivalent playing experience, and it lays the groundwork for those interested in future tournament participation. Participants should bring their own racket, non-marking court shoes and water, and be prepared for a higher-intensity session than typical junior classes. It is a focused, all-girls environment for serious young players wanting to advance.

name: Kids Padel Starters
description: Kids Padel Starters at Baseline Al Majaz is a lively, mixed-gender introduction to padel for children aged 5 to 8. Sessions run Friday evenings from 20:30 to 22:00 under coach Zayed Al Nuaimi, using fun, games-led activities to build basic hand-eye coordination, simple footwork and an early feel for hitting the ball with control. The relaxed, playful format keeps younger children engaged while gently introducing padel-specific skills like short rallies and basic court awareness. Rather than formal drilling, the emphasis is on enjoyment, movement and building comfort on court, making it an easy entry point even for children with no previous racket sports experience. Lightweight junior rackets are provided for those who do not yet have their own. Parents should send children in comfortable sportswear and non-marking trainers, along with a water bottle. It is a cheerful first taste of padel designed to spark early enthusiasm for the sport.

name: Cardio Padel
description: Cardio Padel is a high-tempo, mixed-ability session open to players aged sixteen and above, mixing men and women on court together for a workout built around constant movement rather than technical drilling. Amina Belhaj leads groups through fast rotations, continuous rallies and short-burst games designed to keep heart rates up and rest periods brief, so the emphasis sits on fitness, footwork and reaction speed as much as padel craft. Because the format welcomes all levels, exercises are scaled so beginners keep pace while stronger players get extra intensity through added shot targets or tighter time limits. Expect to finish sweating, having covered plenty of ground and sharpened your court coverage along the way. Bring indoor court shoes, a padel racket if you own one, plenty of water and a towel. This Saturday morning slot suits anyone wanting a social, energetic start to the weekend without the pressure of formal coaching progression.

name: Competition Squad
description: Competition Squad is a demanding, mixed session for advanced players aged sixteen and over who are already competing or preparing to step into tournament play. Under Ricardo Duarte's guidance, sessions focus on match-specific pressure situations, doubles positioning, shot selection under fatigue and the mental composure needed when points get tight. Expect live-ball scenarios, video-style feedback on tactics, and structured points play against players of similar standard, all aimed at sharpening the fine margins that decide close matches. Participants should already have solid technical foundations, since the pace assumes confident volleys, smashes and wall play rather than teaching them from scratch. Bring a racket suited to competitive play, indoor court shoes, water and a positive appetite for constructive criticism. This Friday afternoon slot suits players building toward club leagues or regional events who want focused, accountable practice alongside others chasing the same standard.

name: Technique Clinic
description: Technique Clinic is a twice-weekly, mixed session for intermediate players aged sixteen and above who already understand the basics but want to refine how shots are actually executed. Carlos Ibanez breaks sessions down into detailed work on grip, contact point, footwork sequencing and the subtler mechanics behind volleys, bandejas and defensive lobs, correcting habits that tend to hold intermediate players back. Expect plenty of repetition drills, partner feedback and short explanations of the reasoning behind each adjustment, rather than fast-paced match play. Players leave each session with one or two concrete technical points to carry into their regular games. Bring your own racket if possible, indoor court shoes and water. Running on Tuesday and Thursday mornings, this class suits those who play regularly but feel their technique has plateaued and want structured, coach-led correction rather than general practice.

name: Ladies Morning Social Drills
description: Ladies Morning Social Drills is a relaxed, all-levels class open exclusively to women aged sixteen and above who want to combine steady improvement with a sociable court atmosphere. Coach Zayed Al Nuaimi runs friendly, varied drills covering positioning, consistency and doubles communication, mixing players of different standards so newer members learn from more experienced ones while everyone gets plenty of ball contact. The tone stays encouraging rather than competitive, with regular pauses for tips, chat and rotating partners so the group gets to know one another across sessions. Expect to leave with sharper basics and a few new faces to play with outside class. Bring indoor court shoes, a racket if you have one and water. Held on Friday afternoons, this session suits women looking for a supportive entry point into regular padel practice within a welcoming, women-only environment.

name: Ladies Tactics Workshop
description: Ladies Tactics Workshop is an advanced, women-only class for players aged eighteen and above who already have strong technical games and want to sharpen decision-making on court. Carlos Ibanez focuses sessions on doubles strategy, including court positioning, shot selection under pressure, exploiting angles and reading an opponent's patterns, using structured points play and situational drills rather than basic stroke work. Discussion forms a real part of the class, with pauses to unpack why a particular tactic worked or failed, helping players think more clearly during matches rather than just react. Participants should arrive with confident volleys and smashes already in place, since the pace assumes solid technical grounding. Bring a racket suited to competitive play, indoor court shoes and water. Running Tuesday and Thursday evenings, this workshop suits experienced women players preparing for league or club-level competition.

name: Ladies Adult Beginner Course
description: Ladies Adult Beginner Course introduces women aged sixteen and above to padel from first principles, in a women-only setting designed to build confidence without pressure. Noura Al Suwaidi guides participants through grip, basic groundstrokes, serving, and the fundamentals of using the glass and mesh walls, alongside simple positioning ideas for doubles play. Sessions progress gradually across the course, with plenty of repetition and encouragement so newcomers become comfortable rallying and understanding basic scoring before moving into more structured play. No prior experience is expected or required, making this an ideal starting point for anyone curious about the sport. Bring flat-soled indoor court shoes, comfortable sportswear and water; rackets are available to borrow for those without their own. Running Sunday and Tuesday mornings, the course suits women wanting a steady, supportive introduction to padel alongside others starting from the same point.

name: Ladies Adult Improver Course
description: Ladies Adult Improver Course is a women-only, intermediate-level programme for players aged sixteen and above who have grasped the basics and are ready to tighten their game. Carlos Ibanez works on consolidating consistency, introducing wall rebounds, smash technique and more deliberate doubles positioning, moving participants beyond beginner rallies into more purposeful point construction. Sessions blend drilling with guided points play so new skills get tested under light match pressure soon after they're introduced. Expect steady progression across the course as coordination, shot selection and court awareness all develop together. Bring indoor court shoes, your own racket if you have one, and water for the session. Held on Sunday and Tuesday evenings, this course suits women who've completed a beginner course or played casually and now want structured coaching to close the gaps in their game.

name: Ladies Beginner Academy
description: Ladies Beginner Academy offers a women-only introduction to padel for players aged sixteen and above, run by Shaikha Al Qasimi with a strong focus on building fundamentals in a patient, low-pressure environment. Sessions cover grip and stance, basic forehand and backhand technique, serving, and an introduction to using the court's walls, alongside simple explanations of scoring and doubles etiquette. The pace stays deliberately gentle, with instructors demonstrating each skill before participants try it themselves in small, manageable drills. This academy suits complete beginners as well as those returning to the sport after a long break, since no prior padel experience is assumed. Bring flat-soled indoor court shoes, comfortable clothing and water; loan rackets are available on request. Running Friday mornings, it gives women a relaxed, encouraging space to learn the game's basics before progressing to improver-level coaching.

name: Ladies Social Doubles
description: A relaxed but competitive Friday evening session at Baseline Al Majaz, open exclusively to women aged eighteen and over who already have solid doubles experience. Shaikha Al Qasimi organises rotating pairs across the courts, focusing on the tactical side of intermediate padel: shot selection at the net, communication between partners, and reading an opponent's setup before they strike. Expect rally-based games rather than isolated drills, with Shaikha stepping in between points to suggest positioning tweaks. It suits players who can sustain a rally and want regular match minutes in a supportive, ladies-only environment rather than formal coaching. Bring your own racket, comfortable court shoes, and enough water for a full ninety minutes, as the pace stays lively throughout. Non-marking trainers are required. New faces are welcome provided they're comfortable with doubles positioning already, and the group format means every week brings different partners and matchups to keep things fresh.

name: Junior Academy
description: A twice-weekly introduction to padel for children aged nine to fifteen, held on Sunday and Thursday afternoons at Baseline Al Majaz under the guidance of Zayed Al Nuaimi. Sessions are mixed-gender and designed for complete beginners, covering grip, underarm and overarm serves, wall rebounds, and basic court movement through games rather than repetitive drilling. Zayed keeps groups small so every junior gets hands-on correction, and each session ends with a fun mini-match to apply what's been learned. It's an ideal starting point for children new to racket sports or moving across from tennis, building confidence before more structured technical work. Parents should send juniors in breathable sportswear with court-appropriate trainers, a labelled water bottle, and a rented or personal racket if they have one. No prior experience is needed, and the relaxed, encouraging atmosphere means shy beginners settle in quickly alongside more sporty kids in the same age bracket.

name: Junior Performance Squad
description: An early-morning training block for juniors aged twelve to seventeen who already play at an intermediate standard and want to push toward competitive padel. Held Tuesday and Thursday mornings at Baseline Al Majaz with coach Zayed Al Nuaimi, sessions mix mixed-gender pairs through high-intensity drills covering smash technique, lob defence, and transitioning from defence to attack at the net. Fitness elements are woven in, including footwork ladders and short conditioning bursts, to build the stamina tournament play demands. This squad suits juniors already comfortable with rallying and basic tactics who are aiming for club fixtures or regional junior events. Bring a well-strung racket, two changes of grip if possible, supportive court shoes, and a substantial water bottle given the early heat. A light breakfast beforehand is recommended, as the ninety-minute session is demanding from the first whistle and expects a level of commitment beyond casual junior sessions.

name: Adult Beginner Course
description: A structured entry course for total beginners aged sixteen and above, mixed-gender, running Tuesday and Thursday evenings at Baseline Ajman Corniche under coach Saif Al Shamsi. Across the course, participants build fundamentals from scratch: grip and stance, controlled groundstrokes, serving rules, and how to use the glass and mesh walls that make padel distinct from tennis. Saif paces sessions so nobody feels rushed, mixing short technical explanations with plenty of hands-on rallying against friendly opposition. It's aimed squarely at newcomers, including those who've never held a racket, and by the end participants should be able to hold a rally and understand basic scoring and positioning. Bring flat-soled court shoes, comfortable sportswear, and a bottle of water; rackets are available to borrow for those without their own. Evening sessions make it easy to fit around work, and the course provides a solid foundation before progressing to improver-level classes.

name: Adult Improver Course
description: A progression course for mixed-gender adults aged sixteen and over who can already rally consistently and want to sharpen tactical understanding. Running Sunday and Tuesday evenings at Baseline Ajman Corniche, coach Valentina Cruz focuses on intermediate concepts: net positioning as a pair, lob and smash combinations, defensive wall play, and reading the third-shot decision that shapes most points. Sessions blend guided drills with live points so players can immediately test new patterns under match pressure. It suits those who've completed a beginner course or built experience through social play and now want to close gaps in consistency and shot selection. Bring your own racket if possible, non-marking court shoes, and enough water for a full ninety minutes as the intensity builds steadily through each session. Valentina gives individual feedback during breaks, making this a good bridge between casual social padel and more competitive club-level play.

name: Ladies Beginner Academy
description: A dedicated introduction to padel for women aged sixteen and above with no prior experience, run Sunday and Thursday early evenings at Baseline Ajman Corniche by coach Dina Kamal. The ladies-only setting is designed to remove any pressure around learning something new, with Dina breaking down grip, basic strokes, serving, and wall rebounds in a patient, step-by-step way. Sessions are sociable as much as technical, with participants often progressing together as a regular group and building friendships alongside their padel skills. By the end of the programme, participants should be able to serve legally, sustain a short rally, and understand core positioning as a pair. Bring comfortable sportswear, flat non-marking court shoes, and a water bottle; rackets can be borrowed on request for anyone without their own. It's an ideal starting point for women returning to sport after a break or trying racket sports for the first time in a relaxed, supportive class.

name: Ladies Social Doubles
description: An intermediate ladies-only doubles session held Sunday and Thursday early evenings at Baseline Ajman Corniche, coached by Dina Kamal, for women aged eighteen and over who already rally comfortably. The focus sits firmly on match play: rotating pairs, tactical positioning at the net, and communication patterns that keep a team working as a unit rather than two individuals. Dina circulates between courts offering pointers on shot selection and court coverage rather than running isolated drills, keeping the session feeling like proper competitive doubles. It's suited to players who've moved past the beginner academy or bring equivalent experience from elsewhere and want consistent match minutes in a friendly, women-only setting. Bring your own racket, supportive court shoes, and water for the full ninety minutes, as games run back-to-back with minimal breaks. The changing weekly pairings mean regulars get exposed to different styles and standards, making it a good way to keep improving through varied matchplay.

name: Junior Academy
description: A mixed-gender introductory programme for juniors aged nine to fifteen, held Saturday and Monday early evenings at Baseline Ajman Corniche under coach Hassan Nofal. Designed for beginners, sessions cover the basics of grip, serving, wall rebounds, and simple court positioning through games and light-touch drills rather than long technical explanations, keeping younger participants engaged throughout. Hassan pays close attention to individual technique while keeping the overall session fun and social, finishing most days with a mini-tournament or team challenge. It's an ideal starting point for children with no padel background, including those coming from other sports who want to try something new in a low-pressure group setting. Parents should send juniors in breathable sportswear, court-suitable trainers, and a labelled water bottle; rackets are available to borrow if needed. The early evening slot works well around school schedules, and the relaxed structure suits both cautious first-timers and naturally sporty kids alike.

name: Junior Performance Squad
description: Junior Performance Squad is an intermediate programme for mixed groups of young players aged 12 to 17, held twice weekly at Baseline Ajman Corniche under the guidance of Valentina Cruz. Sessions build on established fundamentals, sharpening footwork patterns, wall play, and shot selection under match-like pressure. Expect structured drills followed by competitive point-play, with video feedback used periodically to highlight tactical decisions. Players will develop consistency off the back wall, smarter positioning at the net, and the composure needed for tournament situations. The squad suits juniors already comfortable with rallying who want a more demanding, performance-oriented environment rather than casual play. Bring a padel racket, indoor or non-marking court shoes, a refillable water bottle, and light layers suitable for warm-up exercises. Parents are welcome to observe from the seating area. Progress is monitored across the term, with coaches offering informal feedback on readiness for competitive entry into club or regional junior events.
