name: Cardio Padel
description: Cardio Padel is a high-energy, all-levels session at Baseline Ajman Corniche designed for mixed groups of adults aged 16 and above, coached by Valentina Cruz. Rather than focusing purely on technique, the class uses padel-based movement circuits, rapid-fire drills, and continuous point rotations to raise the heart rate and build match fitness. Participants will improve lateral speed, reaction time, and stamina while still sharpening core padel skills such as volleys and smash timing. It suits anyone wanting an enjoyable workout alongside their racket development, whether new to the sport or returning after a break. Numbers are kept sociable, encouraging a friendly, encouraging atmosphere rather than strict competition. Bring a padel racket, supportive court shoes, a sweat towel, and plenty of water, as the pace is brisker than a standard technical class. Sessions run in the late afternoon, so light, breathable clothing is recommended for the warmer conditions typical at that time of day.

name: Competition Squad
description: Competition Squad is an advanced training group at Baseline Ajman Corniche for mixed adult players aged 16 and above who are actively competing or preparing to enter tournaments, coached by Saif Al Shamsi. Sessions are demanding, combining high-intensity drilling with structured match play, tactical analysis, and situational scenarios drawn from real competition. Players will refine shot precision, court positioning, communication with a partner, and mental composure under pressure. This squad is best suited to those with solid technical grounding across all major shots who are looking to push their competitive standard further. Coaches may adjust drills week to week based on upcoming fixtures or observed weaknesses. Bring a padel racket in good condition, appropriate court footwear, a water bottle, and a willingness to be pushed physically and tactically. Given the intensity, a light pre-session warm-up beforehand is recommended. Progress conversations are held periodically to help players track development toward specific competitive goals.

name: Technique Clinic
description: Technique Clinic is an intermediate-level session at Baseline Ajman Corniche aimed at mixed adult players aged 16 and above looking to refine the finer details of their game, led by Valentina Cruz. Rather than open play, the class isolates specific technical elements each week, such as the bandeja, vibora, smash mechanics, or wall rebound control, breaking them down through repetition and coached correction. Participants will leave with a clearer understanding of grip changes, swing paths, and timing adjustments that translate directly into match situations. It suits players who already understand basic rules and rallying but want a more analytical, detail-focused approach to improvement. Small group sizes allow for individual attention throughout the session. Bring a padel racket, comfortable court shoes, and a water bottle, along with a notebook or phone if you like to record coaching points for later reference. Saturday and Monday timings make this an easy addition to a weekend training routine.

name: Morning Social Drills
description: Morning Social Drills brings together mixed adult players of all levels aged 16 and above at Baseline Ajman Corniche for a relaxed but structured evening session led by Saif Al Shamsi. Despite the name, the focus remains firmly on drilling fundamentals in a low-pressure, sociable atmosphere, mixing rotating pairs so players meet new partners each week. Expect a warm-up, targeted technical drills covering volleys, serves, and lob control, followed by light-hearted rotational games rather than formal competition. Participants will build consistency in core shots while also improving communication and court awareness alongside varied partners. The class suits newcomers wanting a friendly introduction as well as experienced players after a relaxed midweek session. Bring a padel racket, suitable court shoes, and water, with the evening timing making lightweight breathable clothing sensible. Coaches keep the tone encouraging throughout, making this a popular choice for players who enjoy the social side of the sport as much as the training itself.

name: Adult Beginner Course
description: Adult Beginner Course at Baseline RAK Marina offers a structured introduction to padel for mixed groups of adults aged 16 and above, led by Khalid Al Mazrouei. Across the course, participants progress from grip and stance fundamentals through to basic rallying, serving technique, and simple positioning at the net and baseline. Each session builds steadily on the last, with plenty of repetition to help movement patterns become natural. Learners will finish understanding court rules, scoring, and the shot selection needed to sustain a rally with a partner. The course is ideal for complete beginners or those with only minimal prior exposure to racket sports. No previous experience is required, and rackets can be borrowed if needed. Bring comfortable sports clothing, non-marking court shoes, and a water bottle, as morning sessions can still be warm depending on the season. Coaches keep group sizes manageable to ensure individual technical points are addressed throughout the course.

name: Adult Improver Course
description: Adult Improver Course at Baseline RAK Marina is designed for mixed adult players aged 16 and above who already have grounding in padel basics and are ready to progress, coached by Maya Khoury. Sessions move beyond simple rallying into more consistent groundstrokes, smarter net positioning, early volley technique, and an introduction to lobs and overheads. Players will work on reading their opponents' positioning, improving shot placement, and developing more reliable serves under light match conditions. This intermediate-level course suits those who have completed a beginner programme or played casually and now want a more focused pathway toward competitive club play. Bring a padel racket, appropriate court shoes, and a water bottle, with the evening schedule making breathable clothing a sensible choice. Coaches provide ongoing feedback throughout the course, helping participants identify specific areas to work on independently between sessions. Group sizes remain small enough to allow meaningful individual correction each week.

name: Ladies Beginner Academy
description: A welcoming, ladies-only introduction to padel at Baseline RAK Marina, open to women aged 16 and over with little or no racquet sports experience. Held twice weekly on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons, sessions with Maya Khoury focus on the fundamentals: grip, the underarm serve, wall rebounds, and basic court positioning. Maya breaks each session into short technical drills followed by point-play so new movements are reinforced in a relaxed, low-pressure group setting. Expect plenty of repetition, clear explanations, and steady progress week on week as coordination and court awareness develop. The group is capped to keep coaching attention high, and camaraderie among participants tends to build quickly. Bring court shoes with non-marking soles, comfortable activewear, a water bottle, and sun protection if arriving early. Padel racquets are available to borrow for anyone without their own. No prior experience is necessary, just a willingness to learn and have fun on court.

name: Ladies Social Doubles
description: This intermediate ladies-only session at Baseline RAK Marina gives women aged 18 and above who already understand padel basics a chance to sharpen doubles play in a social, match-based format. Running on Saturday afternoons under the guidance of Maya Khoury, the session blends short tactical pointers with extended doubles games, rotating partners so players face a variety of styles. Expect focus on positioning at the net, communication with a partner, smart shot selection, and reading an opponent's setup rather than pure technique drilling. It suits players comfortable with rallying and serving who want regular match play alongside light coaching input. The atmosphere is friendly and encouraging, ideal for building confidence ahead of club-level matches or social tournaments. Bring your own racquet if you have one, along with court shoes, water, and light layers for the warmer late-afternoon slot. A great way to stay sharp and meet other ladies in the RAK Marina padel community.

name: Junior Academy
description: Junior Academy at Baseline RAK Marina is a mixed-gender programme for children aged 9 to 15 who are new to padel or building early foundations. Coached by Khalid Al Mazrouei across Sunday and Thursday early-evening sessions, the class introduces core strokes, footwork patterns, and court positioning through games-based drills designed to keep younger players engaged. Khalid places strong emphasis on discipline, sportsmanship, and understanding the rules of the game alongside technical basics like the volley and serve. Sessions are structured to gradually increase in complexity, helping juniors build both confidence and competence over consecutive weeks. Parents can expect steady, visible progress and a supportive environment where mistakes are treated as part of learning. Participants should bring court shoes with non-marking soles, a labelled water bottle, sun protection, and their own racquet if available, though loan equipment is provided. This programme forms the entry point for juniors aiming to progress toward more competitive squads later on.

name: Junior Performance Squad
description: Junior Performance Squad is an intermediate mixed-gender programme at Baseline RAK Marina for young players aged 12 to 17 who already have a solid grasp of padel fundamentals and are looking to raise their game. Held on Saturday and Monday mornings with coach Khalid Al Mazrouei, sessions combine advanced technical work, such as smash timing, defensive lobs, and quick transitions between attack and defence, with structured match simulations against squad peers. Khalid tailors drills to address individual weaknesses while reinforcing tactical understanding of doubles play at a faster pace than beginner classes. The squad format encourages a competitive but supportive dynamic, preparing juniors for club fixtures and junior tournaments. Consistent attendance is encouraged to track progression across the programme. Participants should bring their own racquet, court shoes, a refillable water bottle, and suitable warm-weather kit given the early morning heat. This is a strong stepping stone for juniors with ambitions of moving into competitive squads.

name: Kids Padel Starters
description: Kids Padel Starters is a playful, mixed-gender introduction to padel at Baseline RAK Marina designed specifically for children aged 5 to 8. Coach Adam Whitfield runs Saturday afternoon sessions built around games, coordination exercises, and simplified rallies rather than formal drilling, keeping young attention spans engaged while gently introducing racquet control and basic movement around the court. Children learn to track the ball, make simple contact with lightweight equipment, and understand simple court boundaries, all while having fun with peers in a safe, encouraging setting. Adam's approach prioritises enjoyment and confidence-building over technical perfection at this age, laying groundwork for future padel development. Parents should bring court shoes with non-marking soles, a labelled water bottle, sun hat, and comfortable kids' sportswear. Smaller junior racquets are provided for those without their own. This is an ideal starting point for young children being introduced to racquet sports for the first time.

description: Competition Squad is an advanced mixed-gender training programme at Baseline RAK Marina for committed players aged 16 and over targeting tournament-level performance. Led by coach Sergio Lima across Saturday and Monday morning sessions, training covers high-intensity match simulation, advanced tactical patterns, smash and bandeja precision, and situational play under competitive pressure. Sergio works closely with players on refining shot selection, doubles chemistry, and mental resilience during tight points, drawing on a demanding, structured curriculum designed to sharpen match readiness. This squad suits experienced players already competing or preparing to compete in club and regional tournaments, and attendance expectations are higher than in recreational classes. Participants should arrive warmed up, bringing their own racquet, court shoes, water, and a towel given the intensity of the sessions. Feedback is direct and performance-focused, aimed at players serious about progressing their competitive standard. This is Baseline RAK Marina's top-tier pathway for aspiring competitive padel players.

name: Technique Clinic
description: Technique Clinic is an intermediate, mixed-gender session at Baseline RAK Marina aimed at players aged 16 and above who already play regularly but want to refine specific technical elements of their game. Coached by Maya Khoury on Tuesday and Thursday afternoons, sessions isolate individual strokes such as the bandeja, volley, smash, and serve, breaking each down through repetition drills before applying them within live points. Maya provides detailed individual feedback throughout, correcting common technical faults and helping players build more reliable, repeatable shots under match conditions. The clinic format suits those who understand tactics and rules but want a more surgical focus on stroke mechanics than typical social play offers. Small group sizes ensure each participant receives meaningful coaching attention across the ninety minutes. Bring your own racquet where possible, along with court shoes, a water bottle, and suitable warm-weather clothing. This class works well alongside social or competitive play as a technical top-up.
